articles.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother review – Mahershala Ali is a grieving hitman in soulful thriller
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: the two-time Oscar-winner is an unusual killer in a compelling mix of pulpy action and family drama. Latif, the solemn hitman played soulfully by Mahershala Ali, carries diapers in his kill kit.
body: Those contradictions are on full striking display in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’s opening moments, an explosive close-quarters brawl in a restroom, after which Latif uses the baby wipes to clean up the mess he made with that blade. It’s a lovely image, in a film filled with so many, cutting right through the tension within this character. It also feels like a wink to the audience from Ali and writer/director Bassam Tariq, a way for them to acknowledge right off the top the distracting mess made by that other Blade.

Tariq and Ali were collaborating on Marvel’s Blade reboot. Ali was announced to star as the vampire-slayer formerly played by Wesley Snipes all the way back in 2019. Tariq signed on to write and direct in 2021 but departed a year later. Ali recently revealed that, after being strung along for seven years in development, the reboot was not happening. It’s easy to assume that some of the ideas Tariq and Ali had for Blade made their way into this new collaboration, in which Ali gets to finally wield a blade and John Cho, of Harold and Kumar fame, stuns as a vampiric foe. The echoes and parallels are there but minimal, perhaps even coincidental.

articles.title: Trans Pregnancy Drama ‘Aman’ Boards Parallax Films for Global Sales Ahead of Toronto and London Premieres (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: International sales company Parallax Films has boarded “Aman,” writer-director Rahul Roye’s short film about a trans man who discovers he is pregnant on the eve of his gender-affirming surgery, for worldwide sales.
body: Parallax founder Liuying Cao said: “‘Aman’ is an ambitious film, yet one deeply grounded in human emotion. It touches upon the most intimate experiences of an individual life, while never losing sight of the social and political realities – and responsibilities – that those experiences carry. Rather than resorting to slogans, the film reaches the audience through pain that is visceral, embodied, and deeply human. We are especially thrilled to be collaborating with such a beautiful and moving queer film from India.”

The 16-minute film, a U.K.-U.S.-India-France co-production shot in the Hindi and Bengali languages, had previously unveiled Nikkhil Advani and Dominique Welinski as executive producers. It is produced by Apoorva Bakshi for Awedacious Originals, Elle León Nostas for Aymara Films, Neeraj Churi for Lotus Visual Productions, and Tushar Tyagi and Abid Aziz Merchant.

articles.title: Oscars: Philippines Selects Rafael Manuel’s ‘Filipiñana’ for International Feature Race
articles.summary: Rafael Manuel’s “Filipiñana” has been chosen as the official entry from the Philippines in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. It was selected from a shortlist of 8 films. The film is written and directed by Manuel and is distributed by Kino Lorber.
body: Rafael Manuel ’s “ Filipiñana ” has been chosen as the official entry from the Philippines in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. It was selected from a shortlist of 8 films.

Speaking with Variety, Manuel said he felt the golf course was the perfect setting for the film to explore societal inequities in the country. With the very first courses established on American military bases, the local elite eventually took over, making the golf course a center of power.

“When you think about it, it’s a good metaphor for the country in that it’s very large and situated on a very fertile plot of land that’s toiled on and worked on by so many people, but ultimately enjoyed and profited from by only a select few.” That, Manuel said, illustrates the class divide that has been so ingrained in the Philippines.

articles.title: FCC Chairman Slams James Talarico as Running a ‘Hoax’ With Jimmy Kimmel Interview, Which ABC Punted to YouTube, to Get ‘Clicks and Donations’
articles.summary: Brendan Carr, the Trump-aligned Republican chairman of the FCC, accused James Talarico, a Texas Democrat running for the U.S. Senate, of running a “hoax” to garner attention and campaign donations by sitting for an interview with Jimmy Kimmel — which ABC put on YouTube instead airing it on…
body: Kimmel on Wednesday announced on his ABC late-night show that the interview Talarico would be on YouTube and not TV, saying the decision was made “out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas who would have to deal with this nonsense.”

Talarico characterized ABC’s decision to abstain from putting his interview with Kimmel on TV as effectively amounting to censorship by the U.S. government. “Government censorship should be a concern to all of us, regardless of our political party,” Talarico said in an interview Thursday on MS NOW. The Democrat called the FCC’s threats against broadcasters over “The View” and other programming “the most dangerous form of cancel culture.”
After Kimmel’s interview with Talarico was posted Thursday on YouTube, it notched over 5 million views in the first 24 hours. As of this writing, it has racked up 7.3 million views on the platform.

articles.title: Chris Rock’s Hollywood Send-Up ‘Misty Green’ Hits TIFF With Rosalind Eleazar’s Knockout Lead Performance
articles.summary: Roughly two-thirds through “Misty Green,” Rosalind Eleazar takes a breath and lets a rendition of “One Night Only,” from the musical “Dreamgirls,” rip. The characters around her go quiet, and the crowd at the Toronto International Film Festival, where Chris Rock’s film made its world premiere…
body: “It was such a raw and honest take on the darker side of our industry,” Eleazar said about reading the script for the first time (and charming the crowd with her British accent). “She’s such a complex and such a contradictory and flawed character, and I’m sort of drawn to characters that are difficult to love, and the way that Chris wrote the individual relationships with such precision and nuance.”

“The moment I read the script in London, I was desperate to do this part. So I did whatever I could,” Eleazar said, before realizing what she’d accidentally insinuated, since Misty Green will indeed do anything for a role. Rock and the crowd chuckled as she hastily recovered: “Normal things! Just like Zooms and stuff.”

Eleazar — recently named one of Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch for 2026 — is a best actress contender that dares anyone in the room to argue otherwise. Each scene feels fit for her Oscar clip package, much Cate Blanchett delivered in each beat of “Blue Jasmine.” Misty is a fading, award-winning actress clawing back her career, but self-sabotaging along the way. Eleazar plays her with the danger of Pam Grier and the polish of Tracee Ellis Ross.

articles.title: Woman Unknown wins Venice film festival as NAZA takes special jury prize
articles.summary: May el-Toukhy becomes eighth female director to take Golden Lion as Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love and Guardian-produced exposé of Israel’s Gaza killings also awarded. Bold and bravura choices as Venice celebrates A Woman Unknown, Possible Love – and NAZA.
body: May el-Toukhy’s Woman Unknown has scooped the Golden Lion at the Venice film festival, at an awards ceremony that also saw the Gaza documentary NAZA win the jury prize.

Set in the immediate aftermath of Danish liberation from Nazi occupation, the Egyptian-Danish director’s film tells the story of a young housemaid, Marie (Mathilde Arcel), who is about to marry her widowed employer but anxious about him discovering a shameful secret in her past: during the war, Marie had an intimate relationship with a German soldier.
The Guardian’s film critic hailed Woman Unknown as “elegantly appointed” in his review, likening it to Alfred Hitchcock’s Rebecca.

Arcel also won the festival’s best actress prize, the Volpi Cup, which puzzled some critics: usually, Venice doesn’t award more than one prize to a film. Speaking to the press after the ceremony, the jury president, Maggie Gyllenhaal, said they were able to make an exception because the jury’s vote for the Danish actor was unanimous. “She is going to blow our socks off,” she said.
points: Bold and bravura choices as Venice celebrates A Woman Unknown, Possible Love – and NAZA.

articles.title: Bold and bravura choices as Venice celebrates A Woman Unknown, Possible Love and NAZA
articles.summary: After facing heavy criticism over its lack of female directors, the film festival may have redeemed itself with its winners’ list. Woman Unknown wins Venice film festival as NAZA takes special jury prize. Did the Venice film festival just redeem itself on the sexism issue?
body: Having been pilloried for failing to include enough women film-makers, the festival awarded the Golden Lion to Woman Unknown, by the Danish-Egyptian director May el-Toukhy, her gripping and stylish drama-thriller about sexual shame, political paranoia and the return of the repressed in Denmark after the second world war.

It’s a film with an elegant twist of Hitchcock’s Rebecca. A rich factory owner and widower, who preserved his wealth by doing business with the German occupiers, now wishes to marry Marie, the nanny of his infant daughter, played by Mathilde Arcel, who has also won the Volpi Cup for best actress. But this young woman has an awful secret, which arises just as she is taking the white wedding gown of her employer’s first wife to the dressmaker to be altered so she can wear it at the ceremony at her husband’s cold insistence. A very Hitchcockian touch.
points: After facing heavy criticism over its lack of female directors, the film festival may have redeemed itself with its winners’ list.

articles.title: 'She's back': Fans dance, sing and cry after Céline Dion's comeback concert in Paris
articles.summary: Thousands turned out to witness Céline Dion perform in Paris on Saturday, her first show after a six year illness-induced hiatus.
body: Céline Dion's first concert in years delighted fans, with the Canadian singer crying as she made an emotional comeback to the stage.
It was Dion's first full concert in six years after she was diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome, which forced her to cancel tours.
Joyful fans spilled out of the Paris La Défense Arena on Saturday night singing and dancing to her classic hits, while some were still wiping away tears.
Paris correspondent Hugh Schofield went along and reflects on getting swept up in the Dion dalliance that French fans are calling "the biggest comeback since Charles de Gaulle".

articles.title: Critics celebrate Céline Dion's 'high-stakes' comeback show in Paris
articles.summary: The iconic Canadian singer kicked off her long-awaited comeback show in Paris on Saturday, after a six-year hiatus due to health issues.
body: The 58-year-old superstar was diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome in 2022, which forced her to pull back from touring.

Dion, one of the best-selling musical artists of all time, has not performed a full show since a 2020 concert in New Jersey - the last before the Covid pandemic cut her tour short. In 2024, she performed just one song at the Paris Olympics closing ceremony.
Saturday marked the first of Dion's 26-show residency at the Paris La Défense Arena, Europe's largest covered concert arena.
"I made a promise," she told the Paris audience of about 30,000 people in her emotional return.

articles.title: ‘Look Back’ Breakouts Furi Nanase and Rokka Okada on Growing Up on a Hirokazu Koreeda Set
articles.summary: In the coming-of-age drama, the 12-year-old co-stars play aspiring manga artists whose rivalry blossoms into a defining friendship, brought to life via the director’s famously intuitive way with child actors.
body: Like the characters they would ultimately play, child actors Furi Nanase and Rokka Okada could easily have become rivals when they first arrived on the set of Japanese auteur Hirokazu Koreeda ‘s latest acclaimed drama, Look Back. Both 11-year-old fifth graders when filming began, the two actresses came to the film with opposite levels of experience and very different dispositions.

“I remember looking at her on the first day and thinking, Hmm, is she really so good?” says Nanase. “But then we were introduced and started talking, and I was like, wow, this girl is really interesting!”

The pair, who later shared their 12th birthdays on set just one day apart, became instant best buds. By the time of Look Back ‘s well-received world premiere in Venice last week, they had grown inseparable. As a duo, they landed on various fashion outlets’ best-dressed-of-the-festival lists, thanks to their stylishly retro outfits and adorable antics on the red carpet, where they struck coordinated poses and jumped in the air in unison.
The Hollywood Reporter caught up with Nanase and Okada on the Lido the following day for what amounted to their very first interview with the international press.
